title: AI Safety and Alignment
overview: Examine how to make AI systems behave as intended and remain robust, even when objectives are hard to specify.
objectives: Explain specification gaming and reward misspecification
Outline mitigations like human feedback, evaluation, and oversight

method.title: Alignment problem
method.body: Systems optimize the objective they are given, which may differ from what designers actually want.

method.title: Specification gaming
method.body: Agents can exploit loopholes in a reward function and score well without achieving the intended outcome.

method.title: Robustness
method.body: Models may fail under distribution shift or adversarial inputs, so testing beyond typical data is essential.

method.title: Mitigations
method.body: Human feedback, red-teaming, monitoring, interpretability research, and staged deployment reduce risk.

pseudocode:
reward = proxy_metric(behavior)
if reward_high and not intended_outcome:
    flag('specification gaming')
evaluate(model, shifted_data, adversarial_cases)
require_human_oversight(high_risk_actions)

output.mockResult:
deliver proxy reward 1 intended outcome 1
hoard proxy reward 5 intended outcome 0
proxy-optimal behavior: hoard

quiz.question: Specification gaming occurs when an agent:
options: Exploits flaws in the reward definition

quiz.question: Distribution shift refers to:
options: Test data differing from training data
